summary: Initial POC scoping between Redwood AE/SE and Skyline Logistics to decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Focus: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, and security requirements. Customer leans hosted for speed but requires benchmarks to confirm latency/cost; Dedicated considered for steady throughput and cost predictability; Private flagged for data residency and SOC2/audit concerns.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Tom Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Janelle Kim (Redwood CSM), Mark Chen (CTO - Skyline), Leah Ortiz (Head of MLOps), Samir Patel (Infra Lead), Rachel Gomez (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick scoping to pick deployment path. Customer has a mix of batch embedding workloads (route optimization, match scoring) and low-latency chat for drivers. Concerned about PII/residency and predictable throughput.

[00:00] Tom: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm tom from redwood, priya's our se, and janelle on csm. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark: good, thanks. i'm mark, cto at skyline. we've got leah, samir and rachel on.
[00:14] Priya: great. goal today is to scope a POC: success criteria, what workloads you'll run, benchmarks we should run, and then pick hosted vs dedicated vs private. any constraints to flag up front?
[00:29] Leah: yeah, two big ones: data residency for customer PII in manifests, and we need sub-300ms 95th perc for our driver chat path. embeddings batch can be throughput-heavy, about 10k embeddings/day but in spikes.
[00:45] Samir: infra-wise we have AWS, VPCs, and we prefer direct connect for private deployments but not a blocker for initial POC.
[00:55] Rachel: compliance: SOC2 in place, but some customers require additional audit logs and KMS control.

[01:05] Tom: ok that's helpful. quick framing: hosted is fastest to start — our hosted API with model catalog and streaming. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable latency and throughput with lower unit cost at scale. Private gives you customer-managed control plane and network isolation for residency/audit requirements.
[01:30] Mark: what's the usual decision criteria? cost, latency, and data?
[01:36] Priya: yeah usually it's: 1) risk/residency/compliance -> private, 2) throughput & cost predictability -> dedicated, 3) speed to market and minimal ops -> hosted. there are hybrids too: start hosted, move to dedicated, and if compliance requires, go private.

[02:00] Leah: can you give us numbers? like if we need 300ms 95th for chat at ~200 concurrent users, what does that look like?
[02:08] Priya: sure. caveat — exact numbers depend on model, prompt size, kv caching. ballpark: for a rwd-13B-ish model, with 128 token context, 200 concurrent short chats, you'd want dedicated capacity to hit sub-300ms 95th. hosted can hit it but depends on queueing and noisy neighbors; we can run benchmarks to validate.
[02:32] Samir: would quantized 7B help?
[02:35] Priya: yes, rwd-7B-quant can often meet latency with less GPU. tradeoff is some quality delta; part of the POC is to run evals on quality endpoints.

[03:00] Tom: for embeddings: you said 10k/day with spikes — what's the spike profile?
[03:05] Leah: spikes to ~4k in an hour during route rebalances, also periodic batch windows at midnight.
[03:12] Priya: that's OK — batching helps. Dedicated gives predictable throughput for spikes and autoscaling; hosted is fine if the spikes are short and you accept burst throttling costs. we should capture QPS and tail latency in the benchmark.

[04:00] Mark: success criteria for the POC: what do you need from us and what will you deliver?
[04:06] Tom: from redwood: we'll run three benchmark scenarios (chat latency, embedding batch throughput, and mixed load) across hosted and dedicated configurations. we'll provide latency histograms, cost per 1M tokens and cost per 10k embeddings, and a recommendation. from you: representative prompt sets, sample payload sizes, traffic histogram and SLOs.
[04:32] Leah: can you also include model quality checks? we care about hallucination rates for our support chat.
[04:40] Priya: yes, we'll run a small eval set and include qualitative comparisons for rwd-13B, rwd-7B-quant, and any open model you want to test. we'll include prompts you provide.

[05:00] Tom: timeline idea: customer gives artifacts by Friday (2026-03-06), Redwood runs benchmarks next week, deliver results by 2026-03-11, then we have a follow-up to choose deployment path and discuss contracts. does that work?
[05:12] Mark: yes that timeline works for us.

[05:20] Rachel: for private, we need a security deep dive — KMS integration, audit logs, SSO, and network diagrams. can we schedule that?
[05:28] Janelle: absolutely. we'll set up a security deep-dive with our Security team; target early next week (she suggests 2026-03-10).

[06:00] Priya: a few technical details to capture for benchmarking: average prompt length (we need token estimates), typical response length, concurrency profile, and whether you can tolerate partial prefix caching (some user sessions repeat prompts so caching helps a lot).
[06:18] Leah: average prompt ~80 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. a subset of queries are templated customer queries that should hit cache. concurrency for chat ~200 active sessions during peak, embeddings QPS spikes to ~70 req/s during rebalances.

[07:00] Samir: networking question: for dedicated, is the traffic still routed through redwood control plane or can we have direct peering?
[07:08] Priya: dedicated is still managed by Redwood but we can do private peering and VPC peering options for traffic — you keep a degree of network isolation. for full private on-prem, your infra would host the inference nodes and we provide a control plane optionally.

[08:00] Mark: any compliance pre-requisites for private?
[08:04] Tom: main items: SOC2+, KMS/HSM support, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and ability to host in your VPC or on-prem. we'll share our Private deployment checklist and relevant docs.

[09:00] Priya: bench plan detail: 1) chat latency test: simulate 200 concurrent short sessions, measure p50/p95/p99 across models; 2) embeddings throughput: batch vs streaming modes, measure cost and throughput; 3) mixed load: 60% chat, 40% embeddings for 30 minute sustained period. we'll run on hosted (shared), dedicated with 1x reserved pool and dedicated with 2x reserved pool to see scaling.

[09:45] Leah: can you also show cost-per-unit in both scenarios? we need to justify the commit for dedicated.
[09:50] Tom: yes, we'll provide cost models showing unit price, projected monthly cost, and break-even points for commit levels.

[11:00] Mark: what about failover? if dedicated capacity is saturated, can we burst to hosted?
[11:05] Priya: yes, smart routing can fallback to hosted or another compatible model variant. that's a typical config so apps remain up. there's a config for prioritized routing with automatic fallback.

[12:00] Samir: curious about caching — prefix/KV cache. can you explain how that impacts latency/cost?
[12:08] Priya: sure: KV cache stores attention key-value state for ongoing chats; prefix caching stores static prompt parts. Both reduce tokens computed per request. in practice, caching can reduce per-request latency and cost 20-60% depending on repetition. we'll include caching-on vs caching-off runs in the benchmark.

[13:00] Rachel: audit logs: granularity? we need per-request headers and redaction options.
[13:06] Tom: we export request/response metadata with configurable retention and redaction. for private, you can point logs to your SIEM. we'll send the docs.

[14:00] Priya: quick note on quantization: rwd-7B-quant is lower cost and faster but we'll measure quality delta. sometimes quantized 7B is good enough for routing decisions and chat summaries, but we won't assume it for hallucination-sensitive workflows.

[15:00] Leah: for embeddings, we use them in downstream ranking - need near-identical vector similarity. are there known differences between rwd-13B embeddings and 7B?
[15:08] Priya: generally larger models give slightly better embedding quality; however quantization often doesn't break embeddings as much. we will include cosine similarity comparisons on your sample pairs as part of the eval.

[20:00] Mark: ok, let's talk pilot success criteria succinctly so procurement and legal can see it.
[20:08] Tom: proposal: 1) Latency SLO: chat p95 <= 300ms; 2) Embedding throughput: handle 70 req/s sustained with <200ms per batch (or acceptable batching latency); 3) Quality: hallucination rate below X% on your eval set (define X with you, maybe 5%); 4) Security: meet SOC2/KMS requirements or have remediation plan. pass = move to dedicated commit or private discussion.

[28:00] Leah: agree, we should set X = 5% for hallucination, but allow manual review for false positives.

[30:00] Priya: ok we'll instrument benchmarks to produce the metrics and a scoring rubric. we'll also provide the raw logs and plots so you can validate.

[35:00] Mark: procurement question — what does Dedicated pricing look like, and typical commit terms?
[35:08] Tom: shares a high-level: monthly reserved capacity or annual commit options. unit economics improve with larger commits. I'll send a few sample tiers and a break-even grid.

[40:00] Samir: technical deep dive request: can we see kernel-level perf numbers and GPU instance types used for dedicated?
[40:08] Priya: yes, in the tech deep-dive we can share approximate instance types (A100/RTX etc), observed GPU utilization, and kernel choices, though exact details may vary per deployment. we'll include a perf appendix.

[45:00] Janelle: i'll own scheduling the security deep-dive; tom will send pricing and priya will run the benchmarks.

[47:00] Tom: recap of next steps: customer provides prompt sets and traffic histogram by 2026-03-06; Redwood runs benchmarks and sends results and cost models by 2026-03-11; security deep-dive scheduled for 2026-03-10.

[51:00] Mark: thanks everyone, that was helpful. we'll sync after results.
[51:05] Tom: thanks all, speak soon.

Notes on transcription: a few words may be slightly off (model names like rwd-13B sometimes spoken as "redwood 13k").
end_summary: Decision criteria summarized: Hosted = fastest to start; Dedicated = predictable latency & cost at scale; Private = for strict data residency/compliance. POC plan: benchmarks across hosted/dedicated, evals for quality, cost modeling, security deep-dive for private option. Timeline agreed: artifacts by 2026-03-06, benchmarks by 2026-03-11, security session 2026-03-10.
